AUTHOR: Chuang
TITLE: A Feature Learning and Object Recognition Framework for Underwater Fish Images
REGION: Taiwan (Fish4Knowledge); NOAA Cam-trawl mid-water trawl (Alaska Fisheries Science Center)
SPECIES: Top 15 F4K species; NOAA: adult/juvenile pollock, rockfish, eulachon, chum salmon, king salmon, capelin
DATA: Fish4Knowledge recognition dataset (top 15 species, 26418 images); NOAA Fisheries Cam-trawl dataset (2195 grayscale images, 7 species)
V_EV: Sec. VI.A: 'captured by the Cam-trawl system [7] from a mid-water trawl with only simple web patterns in the background and being illuminated by artificial LED lighting'
D_EV: Sec. VI.D: 'A 10-fold cross-validation procedure is applied to train the classifiers.'
R_EV: Sec. VI.D: 'Results of Fish4Knowledge and NOAA Fisheries dataset are shown respectively in Table II and Table III.' (each dataset evaluated separately, no cross-dataset test)
C_EV: Fig. 6 caption: 'Decision rate and exponential benefit vs. decision threshold.'; Table V compares full vs partial classification (PD 4.92%)
E_EV: Sec. VI.D: 'The recognition performance of each algorithm is evaluated through the average precision (AP), average recall (AR) in addition to the accuracy (AC).'
ARCH: Unsupervised non-rigid part model (PFT saliency, relaxation labeling, SIFT + color histogram) + hierarchical partial SVM classifier
METR: Accuracy, average precision, average recall, per-species F1, partial decision rate
NOTE: Classification of pre-segmented fish images; NCLASS 15 for F4K, 7 for NOAA. 10-fold CV unit not stated explicitly; images are trajectory-derived frames (trajectory voting applied), so folds likely image-level — coded k-fold(이미지). Partial classification (indecision/reject option with optimized SVM threshold) coded as C1=Y, C4=Y; Fig 6 threshold curve treated as threshold sensitivity -> C_ALL=P. V3=Y because artificial LED illumination of Cam-trawl stated; low contrast/attenuation only qualitative. NIMG = sum of both datasets.
